title: Build Knot Pairs, a memory game with cards made by code
kind: a game chapter: build one game from each pair, and this pair is chapters 11 and 12
one: You build Knot Pairs in your own project, exactly as it is in Summit Ready, and test it. Then you change it into a memory game on your own topic.

stages.title: See what Knot Pairs does and how a round plays

screens.title: Look at a round of Knot Pairs, from the first card to the score

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know how a round of Knot Pairs plays and how it scores.
Knot Pairs is a memory game. It is on Slieve Lamagan, the second place on the Summit Ready map.
You build one game from each pair of game chapters. Knot Pairs is paired with Pack the Rucksack, so you build one of those two.
First you build Knot Pairs exactly as it is in Summit Ready. Then, in stage 5, you change it into a memory game on your own topic.
A round starts with 16 [[cards|0]] face down, in 4 rows of 4. Every card back shows a coiled rope on a blue square.
Turned over, 8 of the cards show a photo of a knot, and 8 show the name of a knot. Each knot has one photo card and one name card.
You click two cards to turn them over, and that uses one [[try|2]]. If the photo and the name are the same knot, you have found a [[pair|1]].
A pair stays face up with a green border. The box on the right then says what that knot is for.
If the two cards are different knots, both stay face up for 0.9 seconds, so you can remember them. Then both turn face down again.

blocks.p: Each pair is worth 10 points, so 8 pairs are worth 80 points.
If you find all 8 pairs in 12 tries or fewer, you get 20 bonus points, so the best score is 100 points. In 13 to 16 tries, the bonus is 10 points.
When you find the last pair, the Round over box opens 1.2 seconds later. When the rope snaps, the Round over box opens when you click **See my score**.
Either way, the flag on Slieve Lamagan gets a tick on the map.

words: card
One of the 16 squares you click in Knot Pairs. In the code, each card is a button.
pair
The photo card and the name card of the same knot.
try
Turning over two cards in Knot Pairs. This try is part of the game. It is not the C# word `try` from chapter 4.
bin\Debug
The folder inside your project where Visual Studio 2019 puts the program it builds. Summit Ready reads its data, pictures and sounds from there.
zip file
One file with other files and folders packed inside it.
property
A named value that an object carries, such as `Name` on a Knot. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read the value and change it.
constructor
A method with the same name as its class. It runs once, when code makes a new object with `new`.
static
A method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. You call it on the class name, as in `Knot.LoadAll()`.
List
A list that grows as you add to it. `List<Knot>` is a list that holds Knot objects.
continue
Inside a loop, `continue` skips the rest of this turn of the loop. The loop goes straight on to its next turn.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
field
A variable written at the top of the class, outside every method. Every method in the form can use it, and it keeps its value until the window closes.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `cards[0]` is the first card, and `cards[15]` is the 16th card.
panel
A control that holds other controls. `pnlPlay` is the play area that holds the 16 cards.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(47, 111, 143)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
remainder
`%` gives what is left over after dividing. `13 % 8` is 5, because 8 goes into 13 once with 5 left over.
whole-number division
`/` between two whole numbers drops anything after the decimal point. `13 / 4` is 3, not 3.25.
event
Something that happens to a control, such as a click on a button, or a Timer ticking.
connect with +=
`+=` connects a method to an event in code. `card.Click += Card_Click;` means that a click on that card runs `Card_Click`.
handler
The method that runs when an event happens. `Card_Click` is the handler for a click on any card.
Controls.Add
Puts a control that code made onto a window or a panel. Until then, the control exists, but nobody can see it.
sender
Every handler is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to, such as the card that was clicked.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(Button)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a button.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
ProgressBar
A control that shows a bar. `prgRope` is the Rope strength bar, and its length is its Value out of its Maximum.
ToLower
Gives a copy of some text in small letters. `"Joins TWO ropes".ToLower()` gives `"joins two ropes"`.
Timer
A control that never shows on the window. Once started, it runs its Tick method every time its Interval runs out, until it is stopped.
Interval
How long a Timer waits before each Tick, in thousandths of a second. 900 means 0.9 seconds.
Tick
The event a Timer has. Its method runs every time the Timer's Interval runs out.
Dock
A property that sticks a control to one edge of the control it sits on. `DockStyle.Bottom` sticks it along the bottom.
red underline
The wavy red line Visual Studio 2019 draws under code it does not understand yet. Often it means a method you have not written yet.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what each line of `knots.txt` holds.
Knot Pairs gets its 8 knots from a text file, `knots.txt`. The file is already in your bin\Debug\Data folder, because `summit-ready-files.zip` put it there in chapter 2.
You do not type `knots.txt`. You read it here, so that the code in stage 4 makes sense.

knot-bowline.jpg|Bowline|Makes a loop that will not slip.
knot-clove-hitch.jpg|Clove hitch|Ties a rope quickly to a post or rail.
knot-double-fishermans.jpg|Double fisherman's|Joins two ropes so they will not pull apart.
knot-figure-eight.jpg|Figure of eight|Ties a climber into the rope.
knot-overhand.jpg|Overhand knot|Stops the end of a rope slipping through.
knot-reef.jpg|Reef knot|Ties a sling or bandage flat.

Each line is one knot, in 3 parts with a bar `|` between them. `knot-bowline.jpg` is the file name of the knot's photo, in the Images\Knots folder. `Bowline` is the name that shows on the name card. The last part is what the knot is for. It shows in the box on the right after a match.
The other 7 knots
The other 7 lines have the same 3 parts, in the same order.

box.title: If a file is missing or broken

blocks.p: Knot Pairs never crashes because a file is missing. This is what you see instead.
If `knots.txt` is missing, or has fewer than 8 good lines, no cards appear. The box on the right says **Knot Pairs needs 8 knots in Data\knots.txt.**
If a line of `knots.txt` does not have exactly 3 parts, Knot Pairs skips that line.
If a knot photo is missing, that knot's photo card shows a plain white square.
If `icon-rope-128.png` is missing, the card backs are plain blue squares.
If a sound is missing, that moment is silent, and the game carries on.
To put a missing file back, you download the [[zip file|4]] again and paste its folders into bin\Debug. When Windows asks about the files you already have, you click **Skip these files**.
Skipping keeps every file you already have, including any file you changed. Only the missing files are copied in.

code.title: Knot.cs: the Knot class
code.why: You type the 3 properties, and the 3 lines that put a value into each one, because they are new. The rest reads a file the same way as `LoadAll` in chapter 3, so it comes in the copy.
partLines: The class and its 3 properties

`class Knot` starts the class. Each property holds one part of a line of `knots.txt`. `Picture` holds the photo's file name. `Name` holds the knot's name. `Use` holds what the knot is for. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read each property and change it.
The constructor

This part is the constructor. It runs when code writes `new Knot(parts)`. `parts` is one line of `knots.txt`, already cut into 3 pieces at each bar. The constructor puts `parts[0]` into `Picture`, `parts[1]` into `Name` and `parts[2]` into `Use`.
The start of LoadAll

`static` means that you call LoadAll on the class itself, as `Knot.LoadAll()`. You do not need a Knot object first. LoadAll starts with an empty list. `Files.Data` from chapter 2 gives the full path of `knots.txt` in the Data folder. If `knots.txt` is not there, LoadAll hands back the empty list, so the game shows a message and does not crash.
Read every line

The StreamReader opens `knots.txt`. The loop goes round once for each line, until the end of the file. `Split('|')` cuts each line at each bar into `parts`. If a line does not have exactly 3 parts, `continue` skips it and the loop moves on to the next line. Every good line becomes a new Knot, and `knots.Add` puts it on the end of the list.
Close the file and hand back the list
`reader.Close()` closes `knots.txt`, so that other programs can open it again. `return knots;` hands the full list back to the code that called LoadAll.

screens.title: Type the Knot Pairs fields

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, frmKnots has the variables that remember the cards, the tries and the pairs while a round plays.
These variables are called [[fields|11]]. They sit at the top of the class, outside every method, so every method in the form can use them.
Every field below is new in this chapter, so you type every one.

code.title: The Knot Pairs fields
code.text:
// ---------- Knot Pairs ----------
private List<Knot> knots;                  // the knots in knots.txt
private Button[] cards = new Button[16];   // the 16 cards
private int[] knotOf = new int[16];        // each card's knot, 0 to 7
private bool[] isPicture = new bool[16];   // true: photo, false: name
private bool[] matched = new bool[16];     // true once in a pair
private Image[] photos = new Image[8];     // one photo for each knot
private Image rope;                        // the back of every card

private int first = -1;          // the first card of a try, or -1
private int second = -1;         // the second card of a wrong try
private bool locked = false;     // true while a wrong pair shows
private int tries = 0;           // tries used so far
private int pairs = 0;           // pairs found so far
private int maxTries = 24;       // the rope snaps after this many
partLines: The list of knots
`knots` holds the knots that LoadAll reads from `knots.txt`. `frmKnots_Load` fills it when the window opens.
The 4 card arrays
`cards` is a row of 16 buttons kept together, one for each card. A row like this is called an array. `knotOf`, `isPicture` and `matched` are 3 more arrays, each with one value for each card.
The pictures
`photos` holds the 8 knot photos, one for each knot. `rope` holds the rope picture that every card back shows.
The state of a try

`first` holds the number of the first card of a try. `-1` means that no card is waiting yet. `second` holds the second card of a wrong try, so the Timer can turn it back over later. `locked` is true while a wrong pair is showing, so clicks on the cards do nothing.
The counts
`tries` counts the tries used, and `pairs` counts the pairs found. `maxTries` is how many tries the rope holds before it snaps.

box.title: What each card array holds, using card 5 as an example

blocks.p: `knotOf[5]` says which knot card 5 shows, from 0 to 7.
`isPicture[5]` is true if card 5 shows a photo, and false if card 5 shows a name.
`matched[5]` turns true once card 5 is in a pair.
`new bool[16]` starts all 16 values at false, and `new int[16]` starts all 16 values at 0.

screens.title: Type MakeCard, which makes one card in its row and column

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, frmKnots can make one card and put it in the right place on pnlPlay.
The 16 cards sit in 4 rows of 4 on pnlPlay. Each card is 140 pixels square, with a gap of 8 pixels. So each card starts 148 pixels after the card before it.
MakeCard works out a card's row and column from its number, using 2 kinds of sum. `i % 4` is the remainder after dividing `i` by 4. That remainder is the card's column, from 0 to 3.
`i / 4` is the card's row, from 0 to 3. Dividing 2 whole numbers in C# drops the remainder, so 6 / 4 gives 1. Rows and columns count from 0.

MakeCard makes a new Button called `card`. The card is 140 pixels wide and 140 pixels tall.
Where the card goes
The card's left edge is 24 pixels in, plus 148 pixels for each column. The card's top edge is 10 pixels down, plus 148 pixels for each row.
How the card looks
A flat style lets the border change colour later. `ImageLayout.Zoom` fits a picture inside the card without stretching it. The font is for the knot's name on a name card.

This line connects the card's Click event to the method Card_Click. `+=` adds Card_Click to the methods that run on a click. So every card runs the same method, Card_Click, when you click it.

code.title: Card_Click
partLines: Which card
Card_Click runs when the player clicks any card. `i` becomes the number of the clicked card.
Clicks that do nothing

`||` means or. `return` stops Card_Click, so the click does nothing. This happens when a wrong pair is still showing, or when the round is finished. It also happens when the card is already in a pair, or is already the first card of this try.
Turn the card over
The card turns face up, and the flip sound plays.
The first card of a try
When no card is waiting, the clicked card becomes the first card of the try. Then `return` stops Card_Click, to wait for the second card.
Count the try
A second card makes a try, so `tries` goes up by 1. The Tries label shows the new count. The Rope strength bar's Value becomes the tries left, so the bar gets shorter.
Pair or not
When the two cards show the same knot, Match runs. Otherwise NoMatch runs.

code.title: NoMatch and tmrFlipBack_Tick
partLines: NoMatch
NoMatch plays the wrong sound. `second` keeps the second card's number for later. `locked` becomes true, so clicks on cards do nothing while the pair shows. `tmrFlipBack.Start()` starts the Timer.
Stop the Timer
tmrFlipBack_Tick runs when the Timer ticks, 0.9 seconds later. A Timer keeps ticking every 0.9 seconds until something stops it. So `tmrFlipBack.Stop()` stops it straight away.
Turn both cards back
Both cards turn face down. `first` and `second` go back to -1, and `locked` becomes false, so the next click starts a new try.

screens.title: Put your own data file and pictures into bin\Debug

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, your game reads your own data file and shows your own pictures.
Your own files go in the same folders as the Summit Ready files, inside bin\Debug. Your data file goes in Data, your pictures go in a folder inside Images, and any new sounds go in Sounds.

code.title: Use your own data file and pictures
code.text:
string path = Files.Data("elements.txt");
photos[k] = Files.Picture("Elements", knots[k].Picture);
task: Make a text file with 8 lines. Each line has 3 parts split by a bar `|`: the picture's file name, the name, and what the name means or does.
Save the text file in the Data folder inside bin\Debug, with your own name, such as `elements.txt`.
Change `knots.txt` in LoadAll to the name of your text file.
Make a folder for your 8 pictures inside bin\Debug\Images, such as Elements, and put your 8 pictures in the folder.
Change `"Knots"` in frmKnots_Load to the name of your folder.
Put a picture for the card backs in the Icons folder inside bin\Debug\Images. Then change `icon-rope-128.png` in frmKnots_Load to the picture's file name.
Add a line to `credits.txt` for each new picture and each new sound.
code.test: Press F5 and open your game from the map.
code.expect: 16 cards show your own card back. Turning cards over shows your own pictures and names.
code.hint: LoadAll is the only method that opens the text file. frmKnots_Load is the only method that opens the picture folder.

glossary: card
One of the 16 squares you click in Knot Pairs. In the code, each card is a button.
pair
The photo card and the name card of the same knot.
try
Turning over two cards in Knot Pairs. This try is part of the game. It is not the C# word `try` from chapter 4.
bin\Debug
The folder inside your project where Visual Studio 2019 puts the program it builds. Summit Ready reads its data, pictures and sounds from there.
zip file
One file with other files and folders packed inside it.
property
A named value that an object carries, such as `Name` on a Knot. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read the value and change it.
constructor
A method with the same name as its class. It runs once, when code makes a new object with `new`.
static
A method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. You call it on the class name, as in `Knot.LoadAll()`.
List
A list that grows as you add to it. `List<Knot>` is a list that holds Knot objects.
continue
Inside a loop, `continue` skips the rest of this turn of the loop. The loop goes straight on to its next turn.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
field
A variable written at the top of the class, outside every method. Every method in the form can use it, and it keeps its value until the window closes.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `cards[0]` is the first card, and `cards[15]` is the 16th card.
panel
A control that holds other controls. `pnlPlay` is the play area that holds the 16 cards.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(47, 111, 143)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
remainder
`%` gives what is left over after dividing. `13 % 8` is 5, because 8 goes into 13 once with 5 left over.
whole-number division
`/` between two whole numbers drops anything after the decimal point. `13 / 4` is 3, not 3.25.
event
Something that happens to a control, such as a click on a button, or a Timer ticking.
connect with +=
`+=` connects a method to an event in code. `card.Click += Card_Click;` means that a click on that card runs `Card_Click`.
handler
The method that runs when an event happens. `Card_Click` is the handler for a click on any card.
Controls.Add
Puts a control that code made onto a window or a panel. Until then, the control exists, but nobody can see it.
sender
Every handler is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to, such as the card that was clicked.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(Button)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a button.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
ProgressBar
A control that shows a bar. `prgRope` is the Rope strength bar, and its length is its Value out of its Maximum.
ToLower
Gives a copy of some text in small letters. `"Joins TWO ropes".ToLower()` gives `"joins two ropes"`.
Timer
A control that never shows on the window. Once started, it runs its Tick method every time its Interval runs out, until it is stopped.
Interval
How long a Timer waits before each Tick, in thousandths of a second. 900 means 0.9 seconds.
Tick
The event a Timer has. Its method runs every time the Timer's Interval runs out.
Dock
A property that sticks a control to one edge of the control it sits on. `DockStyle.Bottom` sticks it along the bottom.
red underline
The wavy red line Visual Studio 2019 draws under code it does not understand yet. Often it means a method you have not written yet.
